detail.abstract:
The Global Wealth Preservation Index (GWPI) introduces a new analytical framework for assessing long-term national wealth resilience. Unlike growth focused economic indicators, the GWPI evaluates the structural, institutional, and policy dynamics that determine a country’s ability to preserve wealth across generations. Built on five pillars Economic Stability, Governance & Rule of Law, Diversification & Productivity, Transfer Readiness, and Ethical Finance & Sustainability the index integrates over 60 data points sourced from global authorities including the IMF, World Bank, OECD, BIS, FATF, and UNEP.

This paper outlines the GWPI methodology, indicator selection process, scoring model, and weighting system. It further presents comparative pilot results across select economies, showing how differences in institutional strength, governance, sustainability alignment, and intergenerational planning impact national wealth preservation outcomes. Designed for policymakers, economists, wealth managers, and ESG analysts, the GWPI provides a comprehensive tool for benchmarking stability, designing policy interventions, and guiding multi-generational wealth strategies. The study concludes by positioning GWPI as a global standard for evaluating long-term financial resilience, economic governance, and sustainable wealth architecture.

title: From Boardroom Representation to Workplace Leadership: Evaluating the Effects of California's Gender Quota Legislation on Female Career Advancement

detail.title: From Boardroom Representation to Workplace Leadership: Evaluating the Effects of California's Gender Quota Legislation on Female Career Advancement
detail.abstract: Gender quota regulations, widely applied in the context of elected officials, have recently expanded into the corporate sector. While research in this new context has largely focused on firm performance, the effect of these regulations on women's advancement throughout the organizational hierarchy remains unclear. This study addresses this gap by evaluating California's gender quota legislation as a natural experiment. Using an event study and instrumental variable design (2016-2022), I show that SB 826 substantially increased the share of women on corporate boards and, in turn, meaningfully expanded the share of women in the broader workforce, providing evidence consistent with a "trickle-down" effect of board representation on workplace gender equity. At the same time, the share of female executives exhibits a modest short-term decline after policy adoption. Supplementary analysis documents an increase in first-time female board members, suggesting that firms initially complied with the mandate by turning to new or less-experienced female candidates, potentially including those drawn from their own senior ranks. Overall, the findings indicate that SB 826 succeeded in broadening women's representation in the workforce while also generating temporary adjustment costs at the top of the organizational hierarchy. The results highlight both the promise and the complexity of using gender quotas as a regulatory tool to promote workplace gender equity.

title: A Method for Eliciting Truthful Willingness to Pay for Multiple Products
affiliations: Kyoto University

detail.title: A Method for Eliciting Truthful Willingness to Pay for Multiple Products
detail.abstract: We study a practical mechanism that elicits truthful willingness-to-pay (WTP) for substitutable multiple products from the same participants and selects revenue-maximizing posted prices. Participants report WTP for each product, are randomly split into two groups, each group's revenue-maximizing price vector is learned from its own reports, and the learned prices are cross-applied to the other group prior to consummation. If multiple products clear for a participant, the participant chooses one item at the cross-applied price, under a no-cancellation rule. We prove dominant-strategy incentive compatibility (DSIC) under exact cross-application and show that misreports are strictly harmful in singleton-execution cases. We also formalize demand learning (e.g., mixed logit), portfolio revenue maximization, and a built-in ex-post data-consistency audit comparing chosen products to report-implied surplus maxima. The protocol provides an end-to-end, field-deployable alternative to single-product BDM/RSOP-type procedures for multi-product portfolios, without requiring auctions or complex transfers.

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors are employed by Filevine, a provider of legal case management and AI software. While this study evaluates commercial large language models (including those from OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic) relevant to the legal technology sector, the research methodology and data analysis were conducted independently. detail.abstract: Is a contract a moral promise to be kept or an option to perform or pay? While this question has long divided legal theorists between "Holmesian" realists and promissory moralists, it now faces a new "legal mind": the large language model applied to legal analysis. This Article presents a large-scale empirical study of how large language models (LLMs) advise on efficient breach, utilizing 158,388 decisions across five frontier systems. We find that off-the-shelf models exhibit radically different "jurisprudences" of contract. First, we document extreme model heterogeneity: on identical efficient-breach vignettes, baseline breach recommendations span a 96-percentage-point range, from virtually never recommending breach (3.9%) to effectively always recommending it (100%). Second, consistent with behavioral "licensing" effects in humans, the presence of a liquidated damages (LD) clause increases the propensity to advise breach (avg. +8.9 percentage points), reframing the promise as a priced option. Third, role-prompting is unstable: instructing a model to "act as an attorney" shifts advice in opposite directions across model families. We conclude that for firms and courts procuring legal AI, model selection is inevitably a normative choice among competing philosophies of contract law.

detail.abstract: In this thesis paper, we will look at the effect of macroeconomic variables on the stock prices of the BSE SENSEX Index, an index representing the top 70 companies listed in the Indian Stock Market. It is based on the related publications about the correlation of macroeconomic indicators with stock prices in various countries and pinpoints what might contribute to mixed results and inconclusiveness. The study then focuses on the Indian context and analyses the effect of four key indicators: Gross Domestic Product, Inflation Rate (CPI), Interest Rate, and Unemployment Rate on the BSE SENSEX index. This research utilizes monthly data from April 2002 to April 2022 and conducts several econometric tests to examine the hypotheses. Consequently, according to the results of the study, we can state there exists a significant correlation between GDP and stock prices (positive), and between unemployment rate and stock prices but no significant relation between Interest rate, Inflation rate, and Stock Price. This paper examines the consequences of these findings for investors, exchangers, controllers, and approaches who show a desire to comprehend and anticipate the behaviour of the Indian stock market. The paper reports the findings by emphasizing the caveats associated with the methods and pointing out areas where future research may be headed.

detail.abstract:
Jackson Health System, a premier safety-net institution, faces significant financial pressure driven by the high volume of non-acute patients utilizing emergency services—a systemic issue contributing to a recent $809.6 million operating loss. This white paper proposes the "Community Care Alliance," a strategic tri-partite partnership between Jackson Health System, Baptist Health, and UHealth designed to alleviate emergency department overcrowding through a technology-enabled "split-flow" operational model.

Leveraging a unified EHR platform, this blueprint outlines a mechanism to triage stable, non-acute patients to Baptist Health facilities, ensuring patients receive the appropriate level of care while decompressing Jackson’s trauma resources. The proposal includes a comprehensive legal framework addressing Anti-Kickback Statute (AKS) and Stark Law compliance through a "Triage & Transfer Coordination Fee" based on fair market value. This model offers a capital-efficient strategy to ensure long-term financial sustainability for the public trust while generating new funding streams for academic research.

publicationDetails.detailsText: Chapter forthcoming in: Louis-Philippe Rochon, Sergio Rossi and Guillaume Vallet (eds.), Central Banking, Monetary Policy and the Common Good (Edward Elgar, 2026)

detail.abstract: Over the past decade, central banks have assumed an unprecedented role in global economic governance, especially in the backdrop of the multiple crisis that the world has witnessed. Acting with powers that would have once been considered highly unorthodox and exceptional, they have intervened in ways that have stabilized economies while simultaneously raising questions about legitimacy, accountability, and distributional impacts. These interventions have often intensified inequalities and generated cross-border economic spillovers, particularly affecting peripheral economies. This chapter explores the notion of the ‘common good’ as a lens for understanding central banking’s evolving purpose. Rather than offering a single definition of the common good, it examines how this concept has been invoked across historical and institutional contexts to both justify and challenge entrenched power structures. Central banks are framed as political institutions with the power to affect the systemic distribution of wealth and resources within a community, rather than simply as technocratic institutions. Drawing on critical political economy, heterodox economics, and legal analysis, this chapter highlights how laws and institutional frameworks shape how central banks interpret and pursue societal objectives. Focusing on the post-crisis era, this chapter identifies contemporary expressions of common good in areas such as human rights, climate change, and redistribution of monetary power. It concludes that the idea of ‘common good’ must express a subversive agenda that is able to challenge entrenched asymmetries, long-standing dynamics of power as well as articulate an anti-imperial critique of the international monetary system.

title: Stock Market Fluctuations and Household Demand for Insurance in China
affiliations: National University of Singapore (NUS) - Sustainable & Green Finance Institute (SGFIN), Nankai University, Nankai University, School of Finance, Nankai University and

detail.title: Stock Market Fluctuations and Household Demand for Insurance in China
detail.abstract: Do financial market fluctuations affect household demand for insurance? Using 10.8 million policy transactions from a major Chinese insurer (2008-2017), we find that a one percentage point decline in daily stock returns increases insurance purchases by 1.91% the following day. This response is strongest for pure health protection products: medical insurance (2.38%), accident insurance (2.45%), and critical illness coverage (2.58%), which address health risks orthogonal to financial market conditions. Life insurance with savings features shows smaller effects (1.19%). The relationship is immediate (only yesterday's return matters), temporary (effects decay within one week), and reversible (cancellation rates spike when markets recover during the 15-day cooling-off period). Behavioral mechanisms drive these patterns: market volatility increases investor attention and negative sentiment, with effects concentrated among retail investors exposed to low-priced, volatile stocks. Regional and demographic heterogeneity confirm that financially engaged, middle-aged households with discretionary resources, not health-vulnerable populations, drive the response. These findings reveal systematic mis-allocation in health protection markets: financial stress induces emotion-driven insurance purchases that households systematically reverse as anxiety dissipates. Our results highlight the consumer welfare costs of behavioral responses to market volatility and suggest policy interventions including enhanced cooling-off periods, sales practice regulations during market stress, and financial literacy programs that help households distinguish health protection needs from financial market conditions.

title: Climate Shocks and U.S. Bank Stability
affiliations: , Université de Lille, Université de Lorraine and Université de Lorraine

detail.title: Climate Shocks and U.S. Bank Stability

declarations.funderStatement: This research received financial support from the French National Research Agency (ANR) under grant ANR-25-CE26-5668.

detail.abstract: This paper investigates the effects of systemic climate variability on U.S. banking stability using the El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO) as a quasi-natural experiment. In contrast to studies focusing on rare, localized natural disasters, we examine how persistent and spatially heterogeneous ENSO-induced climate anomalies-especially those associated with the often-overlooked La Niña phase-affect banks across the continental United States. ENSO is the most influential source of interannual climate variation on Earth and provides a compelling setting to study the transmission of exogenous physical risks to the financial sector. We construct a 30-year quarterly panel of over 800,000 bank-quarter observations (1994-2023), combining detailed financial data with geolocated branch networks and high-resolution teleconnection estimates of local temperature anomalies. Our empirical strategy combines three key elements: a regime-based climate shock identification grounded in recent climate science, a granular spatial matching of institutions to localized exposure, and a dynamic panel framework based on local projections. Our results show that strong La Niña shocks reduce the distance to default by roughly 20%, with effects peaking between 7 and 11 quarters after the shock. These disruptions operate primarily through rising credit risk, lower profitability, and weaker solvency-particularly in banks with large real estate exposure, broad but climate-sensitive geographic footprints, and sizable balance sheets. These findings underscore the need for prudential regulation to incorporate granular, forward-looking metrics of physical climate risk, especially as ongoing climate change is expected to increase the frequency and intensity of ENSO events.

title: Testing Vertical Relationships in the U.S. Infant Formula Market: Implications for Government Costs and Welfare

detail.title: Testing Vertical Relationships in the U.S. Infant Formula Market: Implications for Government Costs and Welfare

publicationDetails.detailsText: Kilts Center at Chicago Booth Marketing Data Center Paper

detail.abstract: The U.S. Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) provides free infant formula to low-income households, serving around 39% of U.S. infants. As WIC’s single most expensive benefit, infant formula accounts for around half of the total WIC food costs. To reduce government costs, WIC awards exclusive contracts to manufacturers offering the lowest net price (i.e., wholesale price minus rebate) to the government in each state via public auction, effectively creating monopolies in the WIC market. The broader implications of this policy hinge on vertical relationships between manufacturers and retailers, which remain poorly understood. I identify the vertical relationship as best characterized by two-part tariffs (TPT), where retailers decide retail prices and pay fixed fees to manufacturers and wholesale markups are zero. This finding challenges the common but untested resale price maintenance (RPM) assumption in the literature. Counterfactual simulations show that TPT is more efficient than RPM, yielding higher consumer and total surplus while reducing government costs through lower total markups at equivalent net prices. Specifically, under RPM, average retail prices would be 3.8% higher, consumer surplus would be 7.4% lower, and producer surplus would be 2.2% higher under the current design of WIC. These findings demonstrate that conduct assumptions critically shape welfare outcomes.

title: Divide And Sprawl, Decline and Fall: A Comparative Critique of Euclidean Zoning

detail.title: Divide And Sprawl, Decline and Fall: A Comparative Critique of Euclidean Zoning
detail.abstract:
The land use patterns prevalent in the U.S., which flow from what zoning law refers to as “Euclidean zoning,” have fostered a broad range of problems. Requiring low-density development and high separation of uses contributes to urban sprawl, housing scarcity, flight to the suburbs, pollution, loss of wilderness and farmland, racial and socioeconomic segregation, and legal obstacles to effective urban rehabilitation. Moreover, it channels less well-off children into chronically underfunded schools, makes car ownership a requirement to access many jobs, and even works against crime-prevention goals. While Jane Jacobs’ seminal book The Death and Life of Great American Cities inspired the New Urbanism movement, which proposes a different approach to urban design that arguably could solve many of these problems, implementing New Urbanism is difficult in cities that have Euclidean zoning laws – as some 97% of U.S. municipalities do.

This paper argues that the land-use patterns seen in France confirm that New Urbanism works as advertised – in other words, it prevents or solves most of the aforementioned problems – while the legal mechanisms that underlie French zoning law provide a template that American urban planning professionals can use when considering how to change local zoning laws in a way that promotes best practices in land use and urban planning.

detail.abstract: This paper explores the relationship between mental health and post-secondary student outcomes. detail.abstract: Pharmaceutical drug donations are celebrated as a hallmark of corporate social responsibility. To incentivize giving, the US tax code allows tax deductions that exceed the cost of donated drugs. This turns donation into a strategy to maximize profit via tax deductions. We show that this may induce firms to over-donate or donate drugs that are not needed. This generates waste, distorts aid allocation, and reduces government revenue, thereby limiting public resources available for disaster relief and humanitarian needs. We identify several channels that could exacerbate this loophole. Exploring the tax code in 21 other countries, we argue that this loophole exists in many developed and developing countries.

title: A Future European Union 'Quantum Act'? Critical Lessons from the Global AI Governance Debate
affiliations: University of Macau - Faculty of Law

detail.title: A Future European Union 'Quantum Act'? Critical Lessons from the Global AI Governance Debate
detail.abstract: The year 2025 was officially designated by the United Nations as International Year of Quantum Science and Technology (IYQ) to commemorate the 100 years since the initial formulation of quantum theories. In July 2025, the European Union (EU) released its 'Quantum Europe Strategy: Quantum Europe in a Changing World' , which recognizes that 'today we stand at an in ection point, as the global race to harness quantum technologies accelerates, moving beyond the labs and entering real-world applications'. e same strategy also includes the goal to present a proposal for an EU Quantum Act in 2026, similar to the draft AI Act first released in 2021. With many more countries preparing quantum strategies or laws and working on quantum technologies, the terminology of a 'regulatory race' is reminiscent of the language used in the current global arti cial intelligence (AI) debate. Debates about AI have revealed several critical shortcomings that have hindered the development of consistent and adequate legal frameworks governing AI and related technologies at the national, regional and global levels. This article seeks to point out the major shortcomings underlying the present AI governance and regulatory debates and identify the lessons that can be learned for future regulatory debates on quantum technologies and a possible draft 'EU Quantum Act'. In essence, it argues that it is necessary to first develop 'quantum intelligence' or 'quantum literacy'understood as the conceptual and cognitive skills adequate to the challenges posed by quantum technologies-before adopting new laws.

title: Learning When to Nudge: A Dual-Agent Bandit Framework for Behavioral Interventions
affiliations: Mays Business School, Texas A&M University, Cornell University - School of Operations Research and Information Engineering, University of Wisconsin-Madison - Department of Statistics, Duke-NUS Medical School and Harvard University

detail.title: Learning When to Nudge: A Dual-Agent Bandit Framework for Behavioral Interventions

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors acknowledge there are no conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: There is no funding for this research.

detail.abstract: In many intelligent systems, decision-making is shared between two agents: a recommender agent that selects continuous interventions and a nudging agent that controls access to information via limited, costly prompts for user engagement. This structure creates a key information asymmetry, where the recommender operates with delayed data, and its performance depends on the nudging agent's strategic timing of pro-treatment actions-user behaviors that provide no immediate benefits but are crucial for the algorithm's functionality. This paper studies the challenge of optimizing synergy between these agents under limited nudging budgets. To address this problem, we propose a dual-agent modeling approach involving: (i) a recommender agent that makes intervention decisions based on revealed user history, and (ii) a nudging agent with richer, real-time data that decides when to prompt engagement. To establish proper synergy, we develop the Dual-Agent Bandit Framework for Behavioral Interventions (DABBI) that seamlessly integrates optimizationbased nudging mechanisms with contextual upper-confidence-bound procedures. We prove DABBI achieves sublinear regret across practical settings, including noiseless, noisy, latent, and partially observed contexts. We further establish a minimax lower bound for our dual-agent bandit with limited nudging and show DABBI matches this bound. We evaluate our theory using synthetic data and a mobile-health case study.

title: From Subsistence to Nutrition: Household Food Security Dynamics in China
affiliations: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics, Qufu Normal University, Shanghai University of Finance and Economics and

detail.title: From Subsistence to Nutrition: Household Food Security Dynamics in China
detail.abstract: Ensuring household food security is central to achieving the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. Although China has secured basic subsistence and eradicated extreme poverty, its transition from sufficient caloric intake to adequate nutrition is still underway. Using longitudinal data from the China Family Panel Studies (CFPS) from 2012 to 2020 combined with machine-learning-based method, we assess the dynamics of household food security under dual subsistence and nutritional criteria and identify the characteristics of chronic food insecurity households. We find that household nutritional security lags significantly behind subsistence security, and nutritional inequality across households is substantial. Despite generally low levels of food-insecurity risk, 7.05% of rural households experience chronic nutritional insecurity, and some are not covered by existing social allowance programs. Notably, chronic food insecurity also appears among non-low-income households, which indicates that, beyond income adequacy, nutritional awareness and dietary habits play a critical role in shaping dietary outcomes. This emerging pattern of “selective food insecurity” highlights the need for food-security policies that integrate both income-based support and nutrition-oriented interventions. Our findings provide empirical tools for identifying long-term food-security risks and offer policy insights for more effective nutrition-focused policies in China and other developing countries.

title: Crowd-Induced Referee Bias: Evidence from 2.3 Million NCAA Men's Basketball Player Observations
affiliations: Texas Tech University

detail.title: Crowd-Induced Referee Bias: Evidence from 2.3 Million NCAA Men's Basketball Player Observations
detail.abstract: How does social pressure affect expert judgment? I exploit the COVID-19 crowd shutdown as a natural experiment to measure the effect of social pressure on highly trained decision-makers-NCAA basketball referees. Using 2.3 million player-game observations from 2005-2025, I find that referee bias toward home teams shrinks by 40-45% when crowds are absent. In normal seasons, home players receive favorable treatment from referees: they commit fewer fouls and attempt more free throws than away players in the same game. These advantages decline substantially during the 2020-2021 season without crowds. Critically, the effect appears only in subjective referee-dependent outcomes (fouls, free throws), not in objective performance measures (rebounds, assists), isolating the behavioral mechanism. The findings demonstrate that even experienced professionals operating under institutional monitoring exhibit systematic bias when exposed to partisan social pressure.

detail.title: The Effect of Electronic Banking on the Perfromance of Universal Banks in Ghana
detail.abstract: Banks in Ghana are experiencing a major change in their service delivery as a result of the continuous improvement in technology and customer demands. Ghanaian banks have embraced and introduced various channels of electronic banking to improve their efficiency. However, an advancement in technology brings its own challenges. It is therefore necessary for banks to know how each channel of electronic banking delivery service impact on their financial performance. The purpose of the study is to examine the effect of electronic banking on the performance of Universal banks in Ghana. The study uses a time series dataset obtained from Bank of Ghana websites on all the 23 universal banks in Ghana from 2015-2019. The study adopts a pooled Ordinary Least Square Method for the estimations. The study finds that Automated Teller Machine, Pont of Sales, and Automated Clearing House have a positive and significant influence on banks financial performance. On the other hand, the study finds that E-ZWICH and MOMO have a negative influence on banks financial performance, whiles factors such total banks deposit and inflation have a positive effect on banks financial. Based on these findings, the study recommends that the Point on Sales services which rides on the E-ZWICH payment system should be made available and accessible to market women to attract more patronage since the more the users of a particular product or services, the higher the income generated from that services.

title: Resilience as a Double-Edged Sword: Algorithmic Oversight, Employee Awareness, and Psychological Well-Being in the Chinese Context
affiliations: Macau University of Science and Technology and

detail.title: Resilience as a Double-Edged Sword: Algorithmic Oversight, Employee Awareness, and Psychological Well-Being in the Chinese Context
detail.abstract: The pervasive integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into organizations demands a deeper understanding of its impact on employee psychological health, particularly through distinct pathways of control and transparency. Grounded in the Stimulus-Organism-Response (S-O-R) framework, this time-lagged study of 482 managers in China’s manufacturing sector investigates how AI-based surveillance and AI-awareness influence psychological well-being through the parallel mediators of perceived autonomy and psychological distress, and how these relationships are moderated by employee resilience. Results from structural equation modeling revealed that AI-based surveillance undermined well-being by reducing autonomy and increasing distress. Conversely, AI-awareness enhanced well-being through these same psychological mechanisms. Challenging conventional wisdom, employee resilience acted as a double-edged sword: it amplified the positive relationship between AI-based surveillance and distress, and weakened the protective effect of AI-awareness on distress. These counterintuitive findings reveal a “pressure amplification effect,” where resilience may paradoxically increase vulnerability in high-stakes, algorithmically managed environments. The study contributes to the literature by delineating the dual mediating pathways of autonomy and distress, and by contextualizing the complex role of resilience in AI-enabled workplaces. Practically, it underscores the necessity of transparent AI implementation and tailored organizational support systems that move beyond one-size-fits-all resilience narratives.

title: Investigating the Conditions in Which Women GPs Thrive in General Practice: A Realist Review
affiliations: , University of Surrey, , University of York - Department of Health Sciences, , University of Sussex Business School, University of Surrey and The University of Manchester

detail.title: Investigating the Conditions in Which Women GPs Thrive in General Practice: A Realist Review

declarations.funderStatement: This project is funded by NIHR HSDR, Award number: 161818. The views expressed are those of the author(s) and not necessarily those of the NIHR or the Department of Health and Social Care.

detail.abstract:
Background: Women GPs experience higher rates of burnout, anxiety, depression, and slower career progression than men GPs. Women GPs are sought out by patients for specific conditions, which may increase consultation length. This can be a source of job satisfaction for some. However it can also contribute to additional exhaustion and affects career progression, meaning women GPs are at higher risk of leaving the profession. There is an urgent need to identify solutions to retain and support them.

Aim: This review brings together a wide range of evidence to identify the conditions in which women GPs can thrive, to better support them at work.

Design and setting: An international realist review of academic and grey literature across eight databases and Google Scholar.

Method: Following a realist approach, supported by stakeholder and patient involvement, a range of published documents were analysed using a realist logic to identify how, why, for whom and in what circumstances women GPs thrive at work.

Results: A total of 72 documents are included in this review. Sixteen configurations describe the conditions in which women GPs can thrive. Results cover three concepts: ‘Patient-facing work’; ‘Navigating competing roles’; and ‘Sustainable careers, leadership and success’. However, literature also places heavy reliance on encouraging women GPs to ‘fix’ their own circumstances.

Conclusion: This review provides evidence-based recommendations which may be of interest to those responsible for organisational culture within general practices, including (but not limited to) GP partners, and women GPs, who can utilise the recommendations to influence change.

title: The Voice of Emotion: Advancing Marketing Research Through Real-Time AI Emotion Measurements
affiliations: ETH Zurich, TU Dortmund University, Hume AI,  and AI Empathy Research Initiative

detail.title: The Voice of Emotion: Advancing Marketing Research Through Real-Time AI Emotion Measurements
detail.abstract: This paper introduces a novel methodological approach for analyzing consumer emotions through voice, leveraging recent advances in computational psychology and artificial intelligence (AI). While traditional approaches to voice analysis in marketing research have provided valuable insights on consumer emotions, we conceptually argue and empirically demonstrate that AI emotion measurements provide significant benefits to marketing research in studying consumer emotions. That is, this new method offers unprecedented granularity by measuring up to 48 distinct emotional expressions in real-time conversation. Two key methodological benefits of AI emotion measurements for marketing research are demonstrated through pilot studies. First, expanded emotional granularity more than doubles the predictive power compared to traditional emotion measurement approaches, with complex, nuanced emotions emerging as meaningful predictors of consumer outcomes. Second, the sentence-to-sentence measurement capability enables real-time emotional trajectory analysis, revealing dynamic patterns and inflection points that static measurement approaches cannot capture. The pilot demonstrations show how this methodology advances beyond basic acoustic parameters to capture the rich emotional information that voice naturally conveys. The paper concludes by discussing how this methodological framework opens new avenues for investigating the role of emotions in consumer behavior across voice-mediated contexts that are increasingly prevalent in the digital marketplace.

title: Neuropsychological Mechanisms of Emotional Burnout in Volunteers: Social and Systemic Factors

detail.abstract: Emotional burnout is a multidimensional stress-related syndrome increasingly observed among volunteers, especially those working in high-stress contexts. This article examines emotional burnout in volunteers through an integrative neuropsychological lens, emphasizing the interaction of biological, psychological, and social-systemic factors. We adopt a biopsychosocial paradigm to analyze how chronic volunteer-related stress can dysregulate neuroendocrine stress systems and induce functional and structural brain changes, leading to the hallmark symptoms of burnout— emotional exhaustion, depersonalization, and reduced personal accomplishment. We also consider the social and organizational conditions of volunteer work (e.g., lack of support, secondary traumatic exposure) that exacerbate burnout. Materials and Methods: include a comprehensive literature review (2020–2025) of theoretical models and empirical findings on burnout, with particular focus on neurophysiological studies and volunteer populations. Results: highlight neuroendocrine dysregulation (hyperactivation and eventual fatigue of the HPA axis), limbic system alterations (amygdala hyperactivity, prefrontal cortex connectivity impairments), and neurotransmitter imbalances in burned-out volunteers, alongside cognitive deficits (attention, memory) and motivational collapse. Social factors such as role overload, insufficient recovery, and compassion fatigue are shown to synergistically contribute to volunteer burnout. Conclusion: Emotional burnout in volunteers emerges from a dynamic interplay of neurobiological mechanisms and chronic psychosocial stressors. Recognizing burnout as a systemic issue—reflecting both individual neuropsychological vulnerability and organizational context—is crucial for developing effective prevention and intervention strategies. Prospects for Further Research: include longitudinal neuroimaging studies to track burnout and recovery, development of targeted interventions (e.g., resilience training, organizational support systems) to break the burnout cycle, and cross-cultural research on volunteer burnout in differing societal contexts.

title: The Phase Diagram of Debt-to-GDP Ratio and Debt-Financing of Interest
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: The Phase Diagram of Debt-to-GDP Ratio and Debt-Financing of Interest
detail.abstract: This paper proposes an alternative way of assessing government debt sustainability – the time it takes before the government is compelled, if ever, to finance debt interest with additional debt, a condition I refer to as “Defit” (Debt-Financing of Interest, to be distinguish from Default).  Defit occurs when the government’s annual revenue falls short of annual debt interest obligation, which is equivalent to the debt-to-GDP ratio reaching the threshold x/r, where x is the effective tax rate of the government revenue and r the average interest rate on outstanding debt. The paper derives the sufficient and necessary conditions of Defitting, and the formula for time to Defit in terms of observable economic and fiscal inputs. The present analysis departs from the prior literature as it models the joint dynamics of government cash and debt balances, establishing a link between the debt-to-GDP ratio and the debt-to-cash ratio. This approach yields a more precise characterization of debt-to-GDP divergence, particularly in relation to the differential g-r, where g is the nominal GDP growth rate. The result replaces the absolute level of primary surplus with the differential s-r, where s is the ratio of primary surplus to primary outlays.

title: Algorithmic Justice and Social Inequality: The Sociological Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Law and Access to Justice
affiliations: BML Munjal University

detail.title: Algorithmic Justice and Social Inequality: The Sociological Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Law and Access to Justice
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is swiftly reshaping legal systems worldwide, with both exciting possibilities and serious challenges for social justice. This study engages with the sociological implications of decision-making under AI driven technologies in courts, with a particular interest in how algorithmic bias may replicate or exacerbate the status quo of social inequalities. Although AI systems had been heralded in scholarship and practice as neutral and objective technologies, AI-driven judicial and criminal justice systems operate in social contexts and empirical and theoretical critiques demonstrate that the technologies often reproduce social biases by embedding racial, gender, and class biases in automated legal decision-making. This study synthesizes a systematic analysis of AI tool usage in courts and policing, revealing that the choices made by designers of algorithms, as well as the choice of data, is saturated with norms and regulatory power structures that can create injustice and inequity in justice access and outcomes for marginalized communities. Additionally, the study explores the dilemmas of transparency and accountability that have become pronounced with legal decisions using AI, arguing that the lack of transparency and explainability has eroded public trust and the integrity of due process. Drawing from case studies and policy review, the study identified directions for systemic reform while emphasizing the need for participatory governance of law-tech and awareness of the data used in the decision-making process. The results highlight that genuine change demands movement beyond technical fixes to problematize systems of power and exclusion. Ultimately, the work calls for equitable and inclusive AI design, calls for legal regulation, and establishes the need for future sociological research, all to protect justice and human rights in an increasingly automated world.

title: Ramsey and Keynes … and Sraffa and Wittgenstein: Change in Interwar Cambridge Economics and Philosophy
affiliations: Marquette University - Department of Economics

detail.title: Ramsey and Keynes … and Sraffa and Wittgenstein: Change in Interwar Cambridge Economics and Philosophy
detail.abstract: The Ramsey-Keynes exchange regarding the nature of probability is investigated in connection with the development of interwar Cambridge economics and Ramsey and Sraffa's influences on Keynes and Wittgenstein. First discussed are Ramsey's criticisms of Keynes and Wittgenstein; then Sraffa's criticisms of Marshall and Wittgenstein. Ramsey was influenced by Peirce and pragmatism and Sraffa by Gramsci and the theory of cultural hegemony. Ramsey died in 1930 but Sraffa continued to interact with both Keynes and Wittgenstein. After his critique of Marshall he participated in the 'Cambridge circus' and turned to recovering the Classical economics of Ricardo. Keynes's General Theory statement of what the essence of his theory was and Wittgenstein's Philosophical Investigations distinction between rules of language and language-games both parallel Sraffa's Classical outside forces operating in the economic field argument and Gramsci's state power and non-state institutions view. Keynes and Wittgenstein determined the nature of interwar Cambridge economics and philosophy. Ramsey and Sraffa were instigators of this change.

title: Urban Vision Behind Mamdani’s New York
affiliations: Catholic Theological Union, Chicago

detail.title: Urban Vision Behind Mamdani’s New York
detail.abstract:
This article analyzes the historic election of Zohran Mamdani as the new mayor of New York City and argues that his victory represents a turning point in American urban governance. Moving beyond questions of representation, the essay frames Mamdani’s rise as the beginning of a new urban citizenship paradigm—one grounded in shared belonging, civic humility, and the moral responsibility of reconstructing cities from the ground up. By connecting the moment to Mahmood Mamdani’s theory of citizen-making in Citizen and Subject, the article suggests that Muslim and immigrant communities in New York have shifted from being managed subjects to active authors of urban life.

The analysis identifies five intersecting crises—housing, transit, infrastructure, migration, and climate—as the fault lines shaping New York’s future and evaluates Mamdani’s proposed rent freeze, free bus network, and public care model as urgent interventions rather than campaign rhetoric. Drawing on UIC scholar Nik Theodore’s concept of urban precarity, the article argues that Mamdani’s governance philosophy resembles an “urban engineer’s approach,” where technical maintenance and social dignity are inseparable. Ultimately, the piece contends that Mamdani’s New York may become a blueprint for other American cities seeking to rebuild civic trust and redesign democratic life through solidarity, equity, and everyday dignity.

detail.abstract: This paper critically examines Republic Act No. 9003, the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000, which establishes the national framework for sustainable waste management in the Philippines. The critique provides an overview of the Act’s major provisions, including mandatory waste segregation, the creation of Materials Recovery Facilities (MRFs), and the prohibition of open dumpsites. Findings highlight several strengths of the law—particularly its emphasis on community participation, environmental education, and decentralized waste management systems. However, the analysis also identifies key weaknesses, such as inadequate enforcement, limited LGU capacity, and ambiguities in certain regulatory provisions. The paper further discusses the environmental, social, and economic impacts of RA 9003, noting its influence on public awareness and waste diversion efforts. Recommendations include improving enforcement mechanisms, strengthening LGU support, updating guidelines, and enhancing public-private partnerships. Overall, the critique concludes that while RA 9003 is a progressive and comprehensive environmental policy, its effectiveness depends heavily on consistent implementation and improved institutional support.

title: Productivity Progress Drives the Reconstruction of Production Relations—Traditional Models will Inevitably be Swept Away by the Tide of the Times

detail.title: Productivity Progress Drives the Reconstruction of Production Relations—Traditional Models will Inevitably be Swept Away by the Tide of the Times
detail.abstract: The continuous upgrading of productivity is the core driving force behind the transformation of the times, and the dynamic adaptation of production relations has become the key logic for commercial evolution and social development. Takingtheevolutionary relationship between e-commerce and physical stores, the phenomenonof industry involution, and the impact of new-quality productive forces such as AI androbots as research objects, this paper analyzes the adaptation law of productivity andproduction relations: the rise of e-commerce is not a one-way substitution for physical stores, but a commercial form adaptation triggered by the upgrading of productiveforces in the digital era, and the two ultimately move towards symbiotic development; the essence of involution lies in the mismatch between traditional production relationsand new productive forces, leading to resource waste and low efficiency; althoughnew-quality productive forces such as AI and robots will exacerbate adaptation contradictions, they can better promote the reconstruction of production relations in a more efficient and inclusive direction. The research shows that for enterprises, individuals, andthesocial level, the ability of "sustained adaptation to productivity" is the core competitiveness tocope with changes. Dynamically adjusting production relations and realizing their coordinated evolution is the key path to transforming technological progress intoadriving force for commercial upgrading and social progress.

title: The Gaza Mandate: Challenges and Opportunities for the United Nations
affiliations: University of Waterloo

detail.title: The Gaza Mandate: Challenges and Opportunities for the United Nations
detail.abstract: In the context of the UNSC authorization of a Gaza Mandate on 17 November 2025, this analysis begins with a US government memorandum acknowledging that American "morale is deteriorating" due to the people’s perception that the government is “aiding and abetting in the disintegration of the United Nations”. This essay explores the political history of the sixteen previous mandates of the League of Nations, examining their progress, obstacles, the roles of Mandatory powers, the League (as well as the UN), and US involvement which led to varying outcomes. It seeks to elucidate the potential impact of the Gaza Mandate on the Palestine situation and the United Nations. The essay draws on information from the UN, USG, World Bank websites, and relevant academic literature.

title: Understanding Metropolitan Areas and Metropolitan Regions: A Comparative Analysis

detail.title: Understanding Metropolitan Areas and Metropolitan Regions: A Comparative Analysis
detail.abstract: The rapid pace of urban growth in the 21st century has transformed cities into complex and interconnected systems that extend far beyond their municipal boundaries. As urbanisation intensifies, the terminology associated with city expansion-particularly metropolitan areas and metropolitan regions-is frequently used interchangeably, even though they represent conceptually distinct spatial, functional, and governance entities. Understanding the difference between these two frameworks is essential in urban and regional planning, transport planning, public policy, and sustainable development. This paper provides a comprehensive comparative analysis of metropolitan areas and metropolitan regions by examining their definitions, boundaries, functional characteristics, governance structures, socioeconomic influence, and planning implications. Drawing insights from global examples and detailed case studies from India-including Delhi NCR, Mumbai MMR, and Bengaluru BMR-the paper highlights key similarities and contrasts and argues that while metropolitan areas represent the compact, continuous urban footprint, metropolitan regions reflect a broader sphere of economic, functional, and socio-spatial influence extending into peri-urban and rural territories. The study underscores the importance of adopting regionally integrated planning approaches to address contemporary challenges, such as transportation connectivity, land-use fragmentation, environmental stress, and socioeconomic disparities. It concludes by emphasizing the need for coordinated governance models and integrated metropolitan regional planning frameworks to support sustainable urban futures.

title: From Healthcare Accessibility to National Output: How Technology-Driven MRI Improvements Correlate with the Gross Domestic Product
affiliations: Kang Chiao International School Xiugang Campus, MPI Corporation and University of Arizona

detail.title: From Healthcare Accessibility to National Output: How Technology-Driven MRI Improvements Correlate with the Gross Domestic Product

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no conflicts of interest regarding the publication of this article.
declarations.funderStatement: There has been no external funding for this paper.

detail.abstract: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is among the most transformative medical technologies, yet its widespread adoption in routine clinical practice remains constrained by high economic and technical barriers. According to conservative estimates from our research, expanded MRI accessibility is estimated to increase GDP by a range of 0.0095% to 0.0117% in relative terms, reflecting measurable macroeconomic benefits. Recent advances in MRI-such as AI-enabled image reconstruction for accelerated scans, cost-effective manufacturing, and the emergence of portable low-field scanners-are poised to improve accessibility and enhance diagnostic capacity. These advances are expected to correlate with national economic indicators such as the gross domestic product (GDP). This paper reviews recent innovations in MRI and focuses specifically on one economic pathway: how mortality reductions associated with improved MRI accessibility correlate with national economic output through changes in the effective labor supply. Using a health-augmented Cobb-Douglas production framework, a model that incorporates health capital as a factor influencing productivity and output, and integrating data from existing clinical MRI reports into a simplified model, we conservatively estimate that such mortality improvements could generate short-run national output growth consistent with these projections. Although these short-run gains appear statistically modest, the long-term implications are far more significant. Clinical innovations not only improve healthcare outcomes but also create substantial social and economic returns when considered over extended time horizons. Our findings underscore the importance of sustained investment and research in advanced diagnostic technologies such as MRI, highlighting their dual role in promoting public health and driving economic growth.

title: Techno-Economic Assessment of a Decentralized Modular Anaerobic Digestion Network for Waste-to-Energy Applications in Libyan Municipalities: A Case Study of Benghazi
affiliations: Brega Oil Marketing Company

detail.title: Techno-Economic Assessment of a Decentralized Modular Anaerobic Digestion Network for Waste-to-Energy Applications in Libyan Municipalities: A Case Study of Benghazi
detail.abstract: The management of Municipal Solid Waste (MSW) in Libya, characterized by reliance on open dumping and a lack of processing facilities, presents significant environmental and public health challenges. This study assesses the technical and financial feasibility of deploying a decentralized network of modular Anaerobic Digestion (AD) units to convert the organic fraction of MSW (OFMSW) into energy and bio-fertilizer, using Benghazi as a detailed case study. This is the first comprehensive techno-economic study of a decentralized modular AD network in a Libyan city, filling a critical research gap. Based on a documented MSW generation rate of 750 tons/day and an OFMSW fraction of 30%, a decentralized model of 10 modular units, each processing 22.5 tons/day, is proposed. The technical analysis projects an annual electrical energy generation of 13.365 million kWh and a co-product output of 59,400 tons of digestate. The financial assessment, based on a $13.5 million Capital Expenditure (CAPEX) and a non-subsidized Power Purchase Agreement (PPA) price of $0.12/kWh, demonstrates exceptional viability. Key financial indicators include a Net Present Value (NPV) of $19.69 million, an Internal Rate of Return (IRR) of 28.69%, and a Payback Period of 3.46 years. The sensitivity analysis confirms project resilience across multiple adverse scenarios. The environmental quantification reveals that the project avoids 322,784 tons of CO₂equivalent emissions annually, equivalent to removing 70,170 vehicles from roads. The results confirm that the modular AD network is a highly feasible, profitable, and sustainable solution that simultaneously addresses Benghazi's waste management crisis, enhances local energy security, and supports the agricultural sector through the production of bio-fertilizer. The study recommends the immediate establishment of a supportive PPA and mandatory source separation policies to facilitate project implementation. This work represents a scalable model for replication across Libyan cities and provides a framework for national WTE policy design.

title: The More the Merrier? The Dark Side of Frequent Release of Information
affiliations: Kent State University, Nankai University, Central University of Finance and Economics (CUFE) - School of Finance, Central University of Finance and Economics (CUFE) - School of Finance and Central University of Finance and Economics(CUFE), School of Finance

detail.title: The More the Merrier? The Dark Side of Frequent Release of Information

declarations.declarationOfInterest: All user data in our research is proprietary and provided by an anonymous bank. We appreciate comments and suggestions made by Haoyu Gao, Grace Hao, Jun Hu, Yong Huang, Dongxu Li, Xiaoran Ni, David Rokowsi, Guochao Yang, and seminar participants at Kent State University and Financial Management Association 2025 Annual Meeting. All errors are solely ours.

detail.abstract: Using the Automatic Earthquake Information Release System (AEIRS) that China launched in 2013 as a quasi-natural experiment, which disseminates real-time seismic information to the public, we explore the impact of frequent information release on the pricing in the credit markets and whether such pricing is efficient. The results show a significant increase in loan pricing for firms with higher peak ground acceleration (PGA) scores following the AEIRS. Such effect is more pronounced in firms in regions where seismic risk was previously unrecognized. The baseline results still stand with several robustness checks including parallel trend analysis, spatial regression discontinuity design, placebo tests, and controlling for loan demand effect, etc. Moreover, the release of earthquake information does not alter the actual frequency of seismic events, ex-post loan defaults, or corporate fundamentals. The increase in loan pricing is primarily driven by banks’ overreaction induced by the availability heuristic, which in turn hinders corporate capital investment and asset growth. Collectively our empirical evidence reveals the dark side of frequent information release.

title: Lawyers Practising Learning: Re-Shaping Continuing Legal Education
affiliations: The University of Melbourne

detail.title: Lawyers Practising Learning: Re-Shaping Continuing Legal Education

declarations.ethicsApproval: Department of Education Policy and Management, Faculty of Education, The University of Melbourne

detail.abstract:
Lawyers learn at work, a point not adequately recognised by the Legal Education literature. Thus, a workplace, or learning curriculum, for lawyers is often overlooked. There is a concomitant failure to address meaningful workplace learning for lawyers, to improve their operational insight, and to enhance their work-based learning opportunities and well-being. This preferable approach would equip lawyers to become better practitioners and encourage the participation of master practitioners. Many lawyers work as professionals integrated into organisations. Within this context, their management and leadership and learning are seen as an insignificant by-product of their professional legal work. Yet many lawyers undertake this additional responsibility whether they work in formal positions of authority, or not. Here there is a concern that the rhetoric of professionalism is morphing into the rhetoric of work. This situation disregards the reality of how lawyers work and learn together and the non-canonical or emergent nature of much of their management and leadership work. 

This qualitative study investigates the significance of lawyers’ learning at work experiences in shaping their work in managing and leading others and what kinds of educative support will be useful. The method used was an ethnographic interview and observation based study involving two stages and three years of fieldwork conducted in lawyers’ complex sites of practice. It employed a symbolic interactionism research lens supplemented by appreciative inquiry techniques and reconstructive analysis. 

‘Legal Working Culture’, or ‘LWC’, which this research establishes, is a substantial description of lawyers’ values, beliefs and behaviour when working and learning together in legal organisations and institutions. It transcends individual workplaces and draws on contemporary leadership theory to focus on the work and learning, rather than formal organisational roles. Therefore, ‘LWC’ incorporates both ‘professional’ and ‘organisational leadership’ and does not hive off ‘organisational leadership’ as a separate experience because it is closely aligned to the business of law. It incorporates the notion that ‘professional leadership’ can extend beyond the interests of an individual legal organisation.  The findings show that lawyers often have dual identities when integrated as professional workers in organisations and institutions which affect how and what they learn at work. 

The beliefs, behaviours and values of ‘LWC’ are sustained by master practitioners, or ‘Leaderworkers’, who do not necessarily have positional authority in the formal sense, but rather, whose leadership standing comes from their intellectual and personal leadership as they draw strength from their cultural heritage. 

These ‘LWC Leaderworkers’ have an important role in teaching leadership to other lawyers. The ‘LWC Leaderwork (Review and Development) Model’ draws on Clinical Legal Education, informal, social and workplace learning theories and recognises the diversity of interests in legal workplaces. It therefore provides guidance to lawyers undertaking formal and distributed leadership work in legal organisations and institutions and to legal organisations, institutions and Legal Education providers. 

The thesis makes suggestions for promoting the acceptance, appreciation and development of ‘professional’ and ‘organisational leadership’ or leaderwork, in Legal Working Culture.

title: Toward a New Paradigm in U.S. Healthcare
affiliations: and

detail.title: Toward a New Paradigm in U.S. Healthcare

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The authors have no personal or financial relationship with other people or organization that may have or could be perceived to have influenced this study
declarations.ethicsApproval: There are no patients or participants in this paper
declarations.clinicalTrialRegistration: The paper is not a clinical trial

detail.abstract:
The American healthcare system stands at a critical crossroads.  Despite the United States (U.S.) being among the most technologically advanced nations, and the one that spends the most on healthcare in the world, the country continues to grapple with fragmented care, soaring costs, inequitable access, and persistent disparities in health outcomes.  There is an urgent need for a transformative shift, not merely in policy or payment models, but in the very philosophy that underpins its approach to health and healthcare.
This need for reform is evidenced from many perspectives.  The current U.S. health care system is experiencing shortages in both workforce and hospital beds in many locations, with a total absence of workforce and health care facilities in others.  Hospital closures are becoming common, and an even larger number are currently in jeopardy.  This is exacerbated by the current and worsening economic conditions, manifest as declining purchasing power, increasing costs, and impending insolvency of the safety net programs.  All of these trends point to an unavoidable erosion of the current healthcare infrastructure and a future in which the U.S. shall have to strive to provide meaningful impacts on health with only a portion of its previous assets.
This paper proposes a framework for such an approach comprising three major elements: Whole Person Care, Value-Based Incentives, and a National Payment Model.

title: College Education and Elite Longevity in Japan
affiliations: Harvard University - Entrepreneurial Management Unit and Waseda University

detail.title: College Education and Elite Longevity in Japan
detail.abstract: We study the lifespans of more than 40,000 elites in Japan born between 710 and 1912 to trace when longevity first began to rise after centuries of stagnation. Lifespans increased sharply during the Meiji era, over two centuries later than comparable breaks among European elites. College-educated elites lived longer across seasons and regions, implying longevity advantages were broad-based. The association between education and longevity became stronger as human capital, public health, and medical knowledge expanded. To distinguish educational patterns from inherited social advantage, we use surnames associated with hereditary status. Our evidence points to a strong interaction between education and health policy as the modern state emerged.

title: Intraday Time Series Reversal
affiliations: Hokkaido University and Hokkaido University

detail.title: Intraday Time Series Reversal

declarations.funderStatement: Japan Society for the Promotion of Science KAKENHI Grant Number 24K16398.

detail.abstract: This study investigates intraday time series reversal that the overnight return predicts the first half-hour return for U.S. market indices. Intraday reversal strengthens during periods of high volatility, including the global financial crisis and the early phase of the COVID-19 pandemic. In contrast, it weakened after the 2010s and during the later phase of the pandemic. These findings suggest that intraday reversal is associated with the presence of opposing investor clienteles-overnight buying by retail investors and daytime selling by arbitrageurs. Moreover, we do not observe intraday reversal for other ETFs that track international market indices. Finally, we propose investment strategies based on intraday reversal and present that they are profitable for U.S market indices but not for international market indices.

title: Houston's Dirty Dozen: A Report on the Top Industrial Air Polluters

detail.title: Houston's Dirty Dozen: A Report on the Top Industrial Air Polluters
detail.abstract: This report identifies the top industrial air polluters in the Houston metropolitan area by analyzing multiple EPA and state-level datasets. Using data from the Toxic Release Inventory (TRI), Risk Screening Environmental Indicators (RSEI), Enforcement and Compliance History Online (ECHO), Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program (FLIGHT), and the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality (TCEQ), the study highlights the petrochemical facilities that contribute most significantly to air emissions and public health risks. The analysis covers the period from 2018 to 2022 and employs data visualization and cross-referencing methods to assess patterns of emissions, violations, and demographic impact. Findings reveal that a small group of petrochemical companies—led by ExxonMobil Baytown, LyondellBasell Channelview, and Chevron Phillips Baytown—account for a majority of chemical releases in Harris County. The report supports environmental justice efforts and public awareness initiatives for cleaner air and more equitable environmental policies in Texas.

detail.title: Less FCPA, More Global Corruption Fighting Heat? Why Multinationals May Face Greater Non-US Scrutiny Ahead

detail.abstract: The Trump Administration's DOJ has signaled a narrower approach to enforcing the Foreign Corruption Practices Act, focusing on cases that involve clear and substantial threats to US interests. While the practical effects are still evolving, this shift likely means a meaningful contraction (or at least reprioritization) of US anti-bribery enforcement. title: Social Insurance in Incomplete Markets: Evidence from a Public Health Coverage Expansion
affiliations: Indian School of Business

detail.title: Social Insurance in Incomplete Markets: Evidence from a Public Health Coverage Expansion
detail.abstract: I study how financial access shapes households' savings responses to a major public health insurance expansion. Exploiting the staggered rollout of India's Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PMJAY) and household-level panel data from the CPHS, I estimate that the program reduced savings rates by 11 percentage points among households with access to formal banking services and by 21 percentage points among those lacking such access. These effects are concentrated among previously uninsured and high-medical-risk households and are accompanied by sharp declines in informal health-related borrowing. The heterogeneous savings responses are consistent with tighter borrowing constraints faced by unbanked households. A sufficient-statistics approach shows that the relative relaxation of liquidity constraints induced by PMJAY generates a consumption-equivalent welfare gain of at least 0.3 percent for unbanked households, over and above the risk-reduction benefits common to all households.

title: Determinants of Building-Sector CO₂ Emissions in the EU: A Combined Econometric and Machine Learning Approach
affiliations: Unicusano University, Lum University Giuseppe Degennaro, Lum University Giuseppe Degennaro and Lum University Giuseppe Degennaro - Lum Enterprise s.r.l.

detail.title: Determinants of Building-Sector CO₂ Emissions in the EU: A Combined Econometric and Machine Learning Approach
detail.abstract: This paper evaluates the structural, environmental, and climatic factors influencing carbon dioxide emissions from the building sector (CBE) in 27 European Union member states from 2005 to 2023. This analysis uses panel data from the World Bank and four econometric models-Random Effects, Fixed Effects, Dynamic Panel GMM, and Weighted Least Squares-coupled with machine learning and clustering to provide a robust analysis of emissions. The econometric models show that all models support a negative relationship between agriculture, forestry, and fishing value added (AFFV) and forest area (FRST), suggesting that a robust rural economy and substantial natural carbon sinks are accompanied by lower emissions in the building sector. On the other hand, water stress (WSTR), PM2.5 pollution, heating and cooling degree days, and nitrous oxide emissions (N2OP) are found to significantly, yet positively, affect CBE. Tests of diagnostic analyses support Fixed Effects and Weighted Least Squares models, whereas results from GMM models are limited by instrument validity violations. In machine learning analysis, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) models are found to be most diagnostic, with all performance metrics being improved, establishing a prominent role for coal electricity, water stress, agricultural intensities, and climatic factors. Subsequently, a solution with 10 clusters, selected using Bayesian Information Criteria and silhouettes, identified a set of environmental and economic characteristics based on differences between low-and high-emission groups. High-emitting groups result from agricultural intensification, pollution, and low energy efficiency, while low-emitting groups are associated with renewable energy, low pollution, and a favorable climate. This analysis, hence, presents a multifaceted assessment of building sector emissions, with climatic, structural, and energy transition patterns as driving factors for meeting decarbonization targets for the European Union.

title: Time Series Forecasting with ARMA Models: A Practical Guide
affiliations: Neu-Ulm University of Applied Sciences and Neu-Ulm University of Applied Sciences

detail.title: Time Series Forecasting with ARMA Models: A Practical Guide
detail.abstract: The paper offers a comprehensive introduction to ARMA-type models, integrating theoretical foundations with practical forecasting applications. Aimed at researchers, analysts and professionals, it offers an easy-to-use approach to time series forecasting. Multiple model configurations are implemented and illustrated using U.S. consumption expenditure data. To extend the analysis to ARMAX-type models, disposable personal income is included as an exogenous variable. Particular emphasis is given on out-of-sample back-testing and forecast evaluation to ensure most accurate predictions. The proposed approach is adaptable to a wide range of time series applications. By combining methodological rigor with practical insights, the paper supports informed model selection and effective implementation in applied settings.

title: When Dealers are the Gatekeepers: Non-Bank Transmission of Central Bank Intervention
affiliations: Glasgow University

detail.title: When Dealers are the Gatekeepers: Non-Bank Transmission of Central Bank Intervention
detail.abstract:
This paper examines how balance-sheet-constrained non-bank investors influence sovereign bond pricing during market stress. Using the 2022 U.K. gilt crisis as a quasi-natural experiment, we show that when margin constraints bind, sovereign bond prices become demand-driven, and safe asset markets fragment. Central bank interventions stabilize prices not only through direct purchases of eligible securities, but also indirectly, via portfolio rebalancing by pension funds—generating spillovers to ineligible assets and mutual funds.

Exploiting cross-sectional variation in pre-crisis gilt exposure across pension funds and in the intensity and timing of Bank of England purchases, we identify exogenous shifts in effective demand. Combining high-frequency gilt transaction data with fund-level holdings and intervention records, we document that more-exposed funds rebalance more aggressively into ineligible securities, raising their prices. These price changes propagate to mutual fund performance. A simple model formalizes this mechanism.

Our findings challenge the conventional view of government bonds as frictionless benchmarks and reveal a new asset-pricing channel: under stress, constrained non-bank demand governs the pricing of safe assets.

title: Markups and Returns to Scale from Financial Statements
affiliations: Shandong University - School of Economics

detail.title: Markups and Returns to Scale from Financial Statements
detail.abstract: It is well documented that treating revenue as output when estimating production functions can bias the estimated output elasticities and markups. A large literature, following Klette and Griliches (1996), addresses this issue by jointly specifying a demand system and a production function. We show that the identifying power of this approach hinges critically on time-series variation in an aggregate demand shifter and is therefore ill-suited for environments with time-varying production technologies. In particular, when the system includes aggregate demand shocks or productivity shocks common to all firms, the model becomes nearly unidentified and the associated standard errors can become arbitrarily large. Moreover, the commonly used specifications impose strong and largely untested restrictions on the elasticity of demand with respect to the shifter, effectively constraining how firms load on aggregate demand shocks.

title: Saving Rate Heterogeneity across the Wealth Distribution in the United States

detail.title: Saving Rate Heterogeneity across the Wealth Distribution in the United States
detail.abstract: Existing studies on saving rate heterogeneity across the U.S. wealth distribution rely on the synthetic method, which ignores wealth rank mobility. This paper formalizes two mobility-consistent estimators and applies them to Panel Study of Income Dynamics data. The synthetic method underestimates saving rates by more than 100% across most of the wealth distribution and overstates saving rate inequality. The mobility contribution to estimated saving rates is positive throughout and declines with wealth, from over 100% in the middle to 15-32% for the top wealth decile. The mobility-consistent estimates show that saving rates out of labor income and new resources rise strongly with wealth, while saving rates out of wealth and available resources are stable or increase only moderately. The positive relationship between saving rates and wealth is driven predominantly by passive saving: for the top wealth decile, over 80% of total saving consists of capital gains. The paper provides several empirical moments that are of interest to the heterogeneous agent macro literature.

title: Information Processing in Coordination Problems
affiliations: University of Surrey - School of Economics

detail.title: Information Processing in Coordination Problems
detail.abstract: We design an experiment to study how information processing needs affect coordination. Two agents observe public signals before playing a coordination game where the efficient action depends on an unknown state. When agents observe the Bayesian posterior belief, efficient coordination increases by 36.5% compared to when they process information themselves. Yet, even with Bayesian guidance, coordination remains well below theoretical predictions. This suggests that both how agents process information and how they act on it-even when processed optimally-significantly hinder coordination. Observing belief disagreements improves outcomes, highlighting the additional role of higher-order beliefs about others' updating behavior.

title: Stochastic Volatility Modelling with LSTM Networks: A Hybrid Approach for S&P 500 Index Volatility Forecasting
affiliations: and University of Warsaw - Faculty of Economic Sciences

detail.title: Stochastic Volatility Modelling with LSTM Networks: A Hybrid Approach for S&P 500 Index Volatility Forecasting
detail.abstract: Accurate volatility forecasting is essential in various domains, including banking, investment, and risk management, as expectations about future market movements directly influence current decision-making. This study proposes a hybrid modeling framework that integrates a Stochastic Volatility model with a Long Short-Term Memory neural network. The SV model contributes statistical precision and the ability to capture latent volatility dynamics, particularly in response to unforeseen events, while the LSTM network enhances the model's ability to detect complex, nonlinear patterns in financial time series. The forecasting is conducted using daily data from the S&P 500 index, covering the period from January 1, 1998, to December 31, 2024. A rolling window approach is employed to train the model and generate one-step-ahead volatility forecasts. The performance of the hybrid SV-LSTM model is evaluated through both statistical testing and investment simulations. Results show that the hybrid approach outperforms both the standalone SV and LSTM models. These findings contribute to the ongoing development of volatility modeling techniques and provide a robust foundation for enhancing risk assessment and strategic investment planning in the context of the S&P 500.

title: The Identification Power of µ-Strong Concavity Assumptions and Sensitivity Analyses
affiliations: Shandong University - School of Economics

detail.title: The Identification Power of µ-Strong Concavity Assumptions and Sensitivity Analyses
detail.abstract: This paper derives a set of partial identification results for the mean treatment response and the average treatment effect when the µ-strong concavity assumption is combined with the MTR or the MTR-MTS assumption. µ-strong concavity is a generalization of the usual concavity assumption and the parameter µ can be seen as a measure of the strength of concavity. By tuning the value of the parameter µ, a practitioner can conduct sensitivity analyses with respect to the concavity assumption. I illustrate my findings by reanalyzing the return to schooling example of Manski and Pepper (2000).

title: Unified Rough Volatility Framework for Variance-Reduced Pricing and Sensitivity of Path-Dependent and Multi-Asset Derivatives

detail.title: Unified Rough Volatility Framework for Variance-Reduced Pricing and Sensitivity of Path-Dependent and Multi-Asset Derivatives
detail.abstract: This paper develops a unified mathematical framework for variance-reduced Monte Carlo pricing and sensitivity estimation under rough volatility. The framework combines three fundamental components within a single estimator: importance sampling via absolutely continuous measure tilting, low-rank learned control variates based on pathwise feature projections, and smoothed pathwise differentiation for discontinuous payoffs. The resulting estimator is shown to be unbiased, variance-optimal within its projection class, and stable under refinement of the rough Volterra kernel. At the theoretical level, we establish moment bounds for rough volatility driven asset prices, derive optimal control variate coefficients under joint importance sampling, prove robustness with respect to kernel smoothing, and formalize convergence of smoothed pathwise Greeks. A central structural insight of the paper is that rough volatility induces approximate low-rank structure in dominant pathwise features, providing a mathematical explanation for the high effectiveness of control variates in non-Markovian settings. The framework is applied at an abstract level across a comprehensive range of derivative classes spanning equity, foreign exchange, interest rates, commodities, and credit. For each asset class, we characterize how rough volatility amplifies Monte Carlo variance, identify the structural sources of inefficiency in naive simulation, and show how the unified estimator systematically mitigates these effects without reliance on model-specific Markovian embeddings. A cross-asset unification theorem demonstrates that all considered products can be embedded into a common Volterra-driven probability space on which the estimator defines a model-agnostic Monte Carlo operator. The paper is entirely theoretical in nature and does not rely on numerical experiments. Its contribution is the establishment of a single, coherent variance-reduction architecture for rough volatility models that applies uniformly across heterogeneous derivative markets, thereby providing a foundational bridge between rough stochastic analysis and large-scale computational finance.
